[RLOW.5.2.2] The compiler **must** compile a `where` conjunct `s.x ~ /p/f`,
where `s.x` is a slot of the pattern's own schema and the conjunct is decided
([IRET.6.4]), to an alpha regex test on that slot
(`proto/alfa.proto#AlphaTest`, `ALPHA_TEST_REGEX`). Under `linear_scan: false` it
does so only when the slot also declares a `capacity` ([LSTR.11.1],
[IRET.6.2.1]); otherwise the conjunct stays in the join test.

The test's `pattern` is `p` when `f` is empty, and otherwise RE2's scoped flag
group `(?f:p)`, with `f`'s letters. An alpha test carries no flags field, and
the group means exactly what the flags mean: DS's three flags are RE2's inline
flags of the same letters ([LREG.5.2], [LREG.8.2]). The group does not capture,
and an alpha test reads no capture.

A valid `p` does not make `(?f:p)` valid: an unterminated `\Q` quotes to the
end of the pattern and takes the group's closing `)` with it. The compiler
**must** validate the wrapped pattern, and where RE2 refuses it the conjunct
stays in the join test, so the artefact never carries an alpha test its loader
would refuse ([IRET.6.3]).

A `!~` conjunct is not compiled to an alpha test: an alpha test has no
negation, so it stays in the join test.
